review_type: Actual viewing of each final PNG with view_image; individual plot content and legibility checked. SVGs share the plotting code and are hashed but were not independently rendered for this review.
reviewer: ChatGPT-assisted review; not independent astronomical peer review

figures.observation: Both spectra repeat the broad blue troughs and red decline. The signed difference is most negative at the blue endpoint; the separately anchored z difference is larger. Final labels, legend, negative differences and noise ranges are legible. Broad visual agreement alone cannot assign the cause of the residual shape.

Blue flux approaches zero and a negative bin is retained. Different spline spaces diverge sharply in that region; the final plot explicitly flags nonpositive unconstrained multipliers. Shared-gri fits leave a larger z difference. The large fractional amplitudes are weakly constrained and do not establish a calibration error or intrinsic variability.

Redward continua overlap closely; blue structured regions show sizable signed scatter and large error bars. The blue-end smooth projection depends on knot spacing, and z disagreement increases after shared-gri fitting. The displayed supplied-pixel band is conditional and cannot settle the physical cause.

Both inputs contain repeated broad troughs, with lower second-observation blue continuum and close red agreement. The wavelength axis stops near 7570 A. Missing i/z and full colour are explicitly retained in the right panel; no continuation is plotted. The partial spectral domain limits comparisons with complete objects.

A strong archive blue-to-red tilt appears between the two coadds. All three spline spaces show this broad difference; separate shared-gri fits reduce the tilt but retain curvature and z disagreement. Final title/legend explicitly say two disjoint coadd sets, five nights and 18 physical exposures. All y labels are now visible after the layout correction; the plot does not assign a physical or instrumental cause.

All five selected pairs are present, with unavailable J1329 processing/null entries left blank and its different domain labelled. The top legend no longer covers the J1105 supplied-pixel range. RMS, synthetic-null components and limitations are readable; the figure explicitly identifies the sample as purposively selected, not a survey error population.

The 18 source-header points form distinct night groups. The second coadd includes larger seeing and airmass values; SEEING50 is explicitly labelled in arcseconds. The footer identifies bounded header prefixes and states that these conditions do not quantitatively explain the spectral discrepancy.
